title: Japan Got a Better Kingdom Hearts the West Couldn't Buy for 11 Years
hook:
Kingdom Hearts Final Mix hit Japan on December 26, 2002 with the English voice cast, extra bosses and new scenes, and the West couldn't buy it until September 2013. Did you ever import it?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Japan got a better version of the first Kingdom Hearts that the West could not buy for over ten years? The original Kingdom Hearts had only been out for a few months. Then, on December twenty sixth, two thousand two, Square released Kingdom Hearts Final Mix, and it was sold only in Japan. The strange part is the voices. Final Mix used the English voice cast with Japanese subtitles, so Japanese fans could hear Sora, Donald and Goofy speak in English. It also added more optional bosses, extra scenes, and a new difficulty setting. Players in America and Europe read about all of this online and could only import it. That wait lasted until Kingdom Hearts HD one point five ReMIX arrived on PlayStation Three. It reached North America on September tenth of twenty thirteen, and it finally included Final Mix. Reviewers at the time called it the first chance for Western fans to play Final Mix at all. Almost eleven years after Japan, the rest of the world caught up. So if you played the HD collection, you have already played the Japan only cut without knowing it. Did you ever import a Final Mix copy back in the day? Follow for more gaming history.
